| Scene description | • The site is in Hubu Alley Food Street, Wuchang District, a commercial pedestrian environment.<br>• In S11-A-02, black classification bins line the pavement. Some carry ‘Residual waste’ labels. One has foam meal containers stacked above the opening; the others are tidy and not overflowing. Concrete paving and a few weeds surround them.<br>• In S11-A-03, an overflowing black bin with exposed foam containers stands against a white wall beside stone steps on grey paving.<br>• In S11-A-04, an overflowing black bin stands against a grey-brick wall beside a blue metal handcart frame and a ‘Diyi Xiang’ sign. The food-street lanes contain roadside or wall-adjacent bins, catering facilities and miscellaneous items. Foam meal containers predominate in the overflow. |
| Regulatory basis | • Catering establishments and operators should collect catering waste separately from disposable tableware, drink containers, plastic tablecloths and other municipal solid waste, using intact, enclosed dedicated containers at designated locations and keeping their surroundings clean. Wuhan Municipal Measures for Food Waste Management, Article 14, items (1), (2), [D-11-C006](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Catering waste should be handed within 24 hours to licensed collectors or transporters, or sanitation operators under district urban management departments. Wuhan Municipal Measures for Food Waste Management, Article 14, items (4), [D-11-C006](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Failure to provide required collection containers must be corrected; failure to meet the deadline attracts a CNY 50–500 fine. Wuhan Municipal Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 44, [D-06-C010](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Failure to fulfil the ‘three responsibilities in front of premises’ must be corrected; failure to meet the deadline attracts a CNY 50–500 fine. Wuhan Municipal Measures for the Three Responsibilities in Front of Premises, Article 17, [D-09-C009](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Sanitation responsibility areas should be clean, without exposed waste, faeces, wastewater, stains or construction debris, and sanitation facilities should remain intact. Wuhan Municipal Regulations on Integrated Urban Management, Article 34, [D-07-C005](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Major commercial streets should have clean roads, no littering or unauthorised trading on roads, and complete, intact and sanitary public facilities. Wuhan Municipal Regulations on Integrated Urban Management, Article 36, [D-07-C007](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Indiscriminate dumping, scattering or stockpiling of municipal waste attracts CNY 5,000–50,000 fines for organisations and up to CNY 200 for individuals. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 42, [D-03-C007](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Failure to transfer food waste to qualified handlers requires correction and confiscation of illegal proceeds, with CNY 100,000–1,000,000 fines for organisations and CNY 100–500 for individuals. Wuhan Municipal Measures for Food Waste Management, Article 24, items (3), [D-11-C010](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Disposal of waste or faeces at unapproved times or places or by unapproved methods must be corrected and may attract warnings or fines. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 34, [D-02-C008](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv). |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Four overflowing bins and one waste accumulation are identified, mainly involving foam containers beside food-street pavements. No extensive pollution or obstruction is evident, but exposed waste impairs cleanliness and creates sanitation and complaint risks. |
| Impact assessment | Visible effects: exposed waste impairs the street’s appearance; some foam containers are scattered on the ground and may attract insects, cause odours and affect pedestrian experience. Near-term risks: high footfall increases complaints and collection pressure. Delayed cleaning may cause secondary pollution or accumulation and affect nearby businesses. |
| Potential causes | • High catering waste generation may exceed bin capacity or collection frequency, as suggested by foam-container overflow in S11-A-02, S11-A-03 and S11-A-04.<br>• Businesses may fail to classify or remove catering waste promptly: bins labelled ‘Residual waste’ contain many foam containers, suggesting mixed disposal.<br>• Frontage responsibilities may be unmet: scattered waste beside bins positioned against walls or steps suggests inadequate supervision.<br>• Verify collection records, bin capacity and placement standards, businesses’ frontage duties, and catering-waste collectors’ frequency and coverage. |
| Long-term effects | Persistent or recurrent problems could worsen sanitation, encourage insects and odours, impair residents’ and visitors’ experiences and damage the city’s image. Enforcement penalties could increase business costs, while prolonged exposure of waste could pollute soil and groundwater. |
| Recommendations | • Immediate action: empty overflowing bins, collect scattered waste and thoroughly clear accumulation points. Remind businesses to fulfil frontage responsibilities and dispose of waste correctly.<br>• Longer-term action: (1) add or enlarge classification bins, especially in dining areas; (2) increase catering-waste collection to ensure removal within 24 hours; (3) strengthen education and checks on frontage responsibilities, penalising repeat violations lawfully; (4) provide temporary storage points or smart recycling units; (5) train businesses in classification and catering-waste management, including responsibilities and penalties. |
| Priority | **High.** Overflow and exposed waste in a busy, prominent pedestrian street visibly impair urban appearance and present sanitation and complaint risks requiring prompt action. |
